note: TUBA4A variants cause spastic ataxia with cerebellar signs and atrophy, creating high clinical overlap with other spastic-ataxias like SPG7 and spinocerebellar ataxias.

evidence.text: TUBA4A mutations cause a distinct spastic ataxia phenotype that enters the differential diagnosis of complex spastic paraplegias and ataxias, expanding beyond previously known TUBA4A presentations.

source.title: A new genetic cause of spastic ataxia: the p.Glu415Lys variant in TUBA4A
source.quote: The phenotype, not previously described, is that of spastic ataxia. Our findings widen the phenotypic and genetic manifestations of TUBA4A variants and add a new type of spastic ataxia to be taken into consideration in the differential diagnosis.

evidence.text: SPG7 often presents with prominent ataxia or mixed spasticity and ataxia, highlighting the known clinical overlap between spastic ataxias and complicated HSPs.

source.title: Loss of paraplegin drives spasticity rather than ataxia in a cohort of 241 patients with SPG7
source.quote: Patients with SPG7 had a mean age of 35.5 ± 14.3 years (n = 233) at onset and presented with spasticity (n = 89), ataxia (n = 74), or both (n = 45).
